trauma.title: Multi-Trauma from RTC - Motorcycle vs Car
trauma.callReason: Motorcycle accident, rider on ground not moving
trauma.sceneDescription: Busy highway, motorcycle lying on side, car with front damage
trauma.appearance: Blood on face, right leg deformed, unconscious
managementImmediate: CATASTROPHIC HAEMORRHAGE FIRST — CAT tourniquet 5-7cm proximal to open femur bleed (not over joint), note time; wound-pack arterial bleeds — this is step 1 of MARCH, before airway (exsanguination kills faster than airway failure in first minutes)
Manual C-spine stabilisation (selective — rigid collar only if mechanism + midline tenderness + neuro deficit)
High-flow oxygen and BVM if needed — aim SpO2 ≥94% (TBI protective)
Needle decompression if tension pneumothorax suspected (5th ICS AAL, 14G x 8cm preferred per TCCC 2022)
Small-volume Hartmann's aliquots (250mL) titrated — target SBP ≥110 mmHg if TBI (BTF 4th Ed; old SBP >90 is outdated), SBP 80-90 if penetrating without TBI

trauma.title: Head Injury with Skull Fracture
trauma.callReason: Fall from height, head injury, unconscious
trauma.mostLikelyDiagnosis: Severe TBI with signs of herniation
managementImmediate: C-spine immobilization with rigid collar and blocks
Airway management with cervical spine precautions (suction, jaw thrust)
IV access x2 with isotonic fluids (Normal Saline only)
Hyperventilation (ETCO2 30-35 mmHg) if signs of herniation
Mannitol 0.25-1g/kg or hypertonic saline if herniation suspected

trauma.title: Penetrating Chest Wound
trauma.callReason: Stab wound to chest, bleeding heavily
managementImmediate: Apply vented chest seal (HyFin Vent / Russell / SAM) — TCCC 2022 / PHTLS 10 standard. Improvised 3-sided taped dressings are unreliable (fail when wet/bloody) and no longer first-line.

PERMISSIVE HYPOTENSION target SBP 80-90 mmHg (penetrating, no TBI): 250mL Hartmann's aliquots titrated to radial pulse / mentation — avoid large crystalloid volumes (dilutional coagulopathy). Activate Major Haemorrhage Protocol for blood products.
TRANEXAMIC ACID 1g IV slow push over 10 min within 3h of injury (CRASH-2, JRCALC 2024) — then 1g infusion over 8h in-hospital.
Position patient with injured side down if possible
Prepare for tension pneumothorax development — be ready to burp the seal or needle-decompress

trauma.title: Penetrating Chest Trauma - Cardiac Tamponade
trauma.sceneDescription: Patient supine on ground, blood visible on chest
trauma.consciousness: Unresponsive to verbal, responds only to painful stimulus
trauma.mostLikelyDiagnosis: Cardiac Tamponade secondary to penetrating chest trauma
managementImmediate: ABC approach with cervical spine protection
Aggressive fluid resuscitation (NS or blood products)
keyObservations: Beck's Triad: Hypotension, JVD, Muffled heart sounds
Signs of shock: tachycardia, poor perfusion, altered mental status
Pulsus paradoxus: >10mmHg drop in BP during inspiration
redFlags: Cardiac tamponade - clinical diagnosis, DO NOT wait for confirmation
Patient rapidly deteriorating toward cardiac arrest
Possible cardiac injury based on wound location

trauma.title: Blunt Chest Trauma - Tension Pneumothorax with Flail Chest
trauma.callReason: MVC - driver trapped, chest injury, difficulty breathing
trauma.sceneDescription: Vehicle with significant front-end damage, driver pinned by steering wheel
trauma.appearance: Diaphoretic, cyanotic, anxious, using accessory muscles
trauma.mostLikelyDiagnosis: Right-sided Tension Pneumothorax with Flail Chest
managementImmediate: IMMEDIATE needle decompression right 2nd ICS midclavicular
Consider finger thoracostomy if needle fails
Coordinate with fire department for safe extrication
keyObservations: Absent breath sounds on right side
Tracheal deviation to LEFT (away from affected side)
JVD bilaterally elevated (impaired RV filling from rising intrathoracic pressure — both jugulars distend, not just the contralateral one)
Flail segment right anterior chest ribs 3-5
redFlags: Tension pneumothorax - clinical diagnosis, decompress immediately!
Tracheal deviation is LATE sign - do not wait for it!
Flail chest indicates severe chest wall trauma
High risk of deterioration during extrication

trauma.title: Massive Hemothorax - Penetrating Trauma
trauma.callReason: Multiple GSW victims, one with chest wounds
managementImmediate: Tranexamic acid (TXA) 1g IV within 3 hours of injury — CRASH-2 evidence for mortality benefit in bleeding trauma patients
Permissive hypotension (SBP 80-90 mmHg if no TBI) via small-volume fluid titration + early blood products
keyObservations: Dullness to percussion (blood in pleural space)
Chest tube output >1500mL indicates massive hemothorax
trauma.environment: Indoor nightclub, loud music, flashing lights

trauma.title: Blunt Abdominal Trauma - Splenic Laceration

trauma.sceneDescription: Vehicle with front-end damage, driver out of vehicle
trauma.mostLikelyDiagnosis: Blunt splenic injury with internal hemorrhage
managementImmediate: Tranexamic acid (TXA) 1g IV within 3 hours of injury — CRASH-2 mortality benefit for bleeding trauma
Fluid resuscitation (permissive hypotension if no TBI)
redFlags: Solid organ injury - spleen most commonly injured
Seatbelt sign = high risk for hollow viscus injury
FAST positive requires urgent surgical consultation

trauma.title: Pelvic Fracture with Hemorrhagic Shock
trauma.callReason: Pedestrian struck by car, pelvic pain
trauma.sceneDescription: Female pedestrian lying supine in the kerbside lane of a four-lane road. Left leg visibly shortened and externally rotated at the hip — foot turned outward roughly 45°. Patient is moaning, conscious but pale. A handbag and one sandal are on the road ~5m up-traffic, marking the impact point. The striking vehicle (silver sedan) is stopped 20m further with hazard lights on; driver standing nearby, visibly shaken. A small blood pool is forming under the left buttock. Bystanders have placed a hi-vis vest beside the patient. No fluid leaking from ears or nose; no head laceration visible.
trauma.mostLikelyDiagnosis: Unstable pelvic fracture with hemorrhagic shock
managementImmediate: Tranexamic acid (TXA) 1g IV within 3 hours of injury — CRASH-2 mortality benefit for haemorrhagic shock
Permissive hypotension (SBP 80-90 mmHg if no TBI) via small-volume fluid titration + early blood products
DO NOT insert Foley catheter if blood at meatus
keyObservations: Blood at urethral meatus = urethral injury
redFlags: Pelvic fracture can lose 2-3L of blood!
Blood at meatus = urethral injury - DO NOT insert Foley!
Pelvic binder reduces bleeding by tamponade effect
High mortality with unstable pelvic fractures
hazards: Glass and vehicle debris on road
trauma.environment: Nighttime, street lighting from overhead lamp ~3m away; warm and humid; asphalt road surface dry

trauma.title: Severe Head Injury - Epidural Hematoma
trauma.sceneDescription: Construction site, patient supine near scaffolding
trauma.mostLikelyDiagnosis: Acute Epidural Hematoma with Uncal Herniation
managementImmediate: Mannitol 0.5-1g/kg if herniation signs (4th-year scope only)
keyObservations: Lucid interval followed by deterioration (classic for EDH)
Cushing's triad: bradycardia, hypertension, irregular respirations
Dilated fixed pupil on side of hematoma
redFlags: Lucid interval is classic for EDH but absent in 30%

trauma.title: Cervical Spinal Cord Injury - Diving Accident
trauma.callReason: Diving accident, cannot move arms or legs
trauma.sceneDescription: Beach, patient supine in shallow water
trauma.appearance: Alert, anxious, appears unable to move below shoulders
trauma.mostLikelyDiagnosis: Complete C5 Spinal Cord Injury with Neurogenic Shock
keyObservations: Complete spinal cord injury at C5 level
redFlags: C5 level = biceps present, wrist/hand function absent
Complete cord injury has poor prognosis for recovery
Risk of respiratory failure if injury ascends

trauma.title: Pneumothorax After Chest Trauma
trauma.callReason: Man fell from ladder, chest pain, difficulty breathing
trauma.sceneDescription: Construction site, patient on ground near scaffolding
managementImmediate: Immediate needle decompression — PREFERRED site 4th-5th ICS anterior-to-mid axillary line (TCCC 2022); 2nd ICS mid-clavicular is a valid alternate but fails in >30% of adults (chest-wall thickness, great-vessel proximity)
Use 14G x 8cm catheter (5cm catheters demonstrably fail in ~1/3 of adults)
Small-volume Hartmann's titration if hypotensive — target SBP 80-90 (permissive hypotension if no TBI)
Selective C-spine per NEXUS/CCR — rigid collar only if mechanism + midline tenderness + neuro deficit
Vented chest seal (HyFin Vent / Russell) if open pneumothorax

trauma.title: Amputation Injury Industrial Accident
trauma.callReason: Hand caught in machine, hand severed, heavy bleeding
trauma.appearance: Pale, anxious, coworker applying ineffective pressure to active arterial bleeding
managementImmediate: Haemorrhage control — apply tourniquet 5-7cm proximal to amputation site; apply tight with one-handed windlass; note time applied
Direct pressure to stump if tourniquet not immediately available — use haemostatic dressing (QuikClot, Celox)
IV access x2 (14-16G) large bore, antecubital
Fluid resuscitation 500mL NS bolus — reassess BP; target SBP >90
Preserve the amputated part: wrap in moist sterile gauze, place in sealed waterproof bag, then place bag in container of ice water — do NOT place directly on ice or submerge in water
Label the bag with patient name, time of amputation, and time placed on ice
Analgesia — Morphine 0.1mg/kg IV titrated; Ketamine 0.3mg/kg IV if haemodynamically compromised
Reassess tourniquet effectiveness — proximal pulse should be absent, bleeding should be controlled

trauma.title: Adolescent - Wrist Fracture from Bicycle Fall
trauma.sceneDescription: Park pathway, patient sitting on grass verge beside bicycle, holding left wrist
trauma.position: Sitting on grass, supporting left wrist with right hand
trauma.appearance: Pale, guarding injured wrist, some tears but trying to be brave
trauma.mostLikelyDiagnosis: Closed distal radius fracture (Colles-type) from FOOSH mechanism
managementImmediate: Scene safety - move bicycle off path
Assess for other injuries (full body check)
Neurovascular assessment of injured hand: pulses, sensation, movement
keyObservations: Low energy mechanism, helmet worn, no other injuries
redFlags: Open fracture (skin broken over fracture site)
Compartment syndrome signs (pain out of proportion, pain with passive stretch)
trauma.environment: Outdoor park, dry weather, warm afternoon

trauma.title: Adult - Minor Road Traffic Collision with Neck Pain
trauma.location: Main road, vehicles pulled over to hard shoulder
trauma.callReason: 30-year-old male, rear-ended at low speed, complaining of neck pain
trauma.sceneDescription: Two-vehicle rear-end collision on main road, minor vehicle damage, patient still in driver seat
trauma.position: Seated in driver seat with seatbelt on
trauma.appearance: Anxious but not distressed, holding posterior neck
managementImmediate: Scene safety - protect from traffic, hi-vis, cones
Full neurological assessment: power, sensation, reflexes
Canadian C-Spine Rules or NEXUS criteria assessment

trauma.title: Teenager - Deformed Lower Leg After Football Tackle
trauma.callReason: 17-year-old, twisted leg in football, obvious deformity, severe pain
trauma.sceneDescription: Astroturf pitch, patient on the ground holding right lower leg, teammates around
trauma.appearance: Pale, sweating with pain, obvious mid-shaft deformity
managementImmediate: Check and document distal pulses, sensation, capillary refill BEFORE and AFTER any movement
Analgesia (paracetamol and titrated stronger analgesia per protocol)
Align and splint in position of comfort
redFlags: Increasing pain out of proportion (compartment syndrome)
